Maritime Law Maritime law is an exciting, dynamic, and rewarding field to practice in. It is also incredibly demanding, involving fast -paced, high stakes litigation and encompassing areas with important economic and policy implications for South Africa. Maritime law has an ancient history, and a number of concepts unique in law. Maritime law first took the form of early maritime codes developed by the various seafaring nations. These principles of ancient origin remain the bedrock of modern maritime law. For example, we will study the principles relating to piracy and the right to arrest a ship. Maritime law remains in many ways a truly international field of law. The United Nations, the International Maritime Organisation, and other international bodies like the Comitè Maritime International have been instrumental in bringing into force a number of international conventions in the field of shipping, carriage of goods by sea, safety of life at sea, and the marine environment. The focus of this course will be on those Conventions which have been ratified or adopted by South Africa as part of our domestic law.
